---
title: "Week 14: Speaking Truth to Power"
---

## Theme: Policy Briefs, Stakeholder Presentations, and Legal Advocacy

Data that never leaves the research file cabinet changes nothing. This
week we shift from analysis to advocacy. We screen and discuss selected
Assignment 4 community data story presentations as case studies in
science communication. Peer evaluation of Assignment 4 is due this week.
We begin curating and polishing the Final Portfolio.

## Classroom Lab Demonstration

**Legal Focus:** Legislative lobbying disclosure rules for 501(c)(3)
organizations (IRS 501(h) election); the distinction between lobbying
(restricted) and advocacy (permissible for nonprofits); community
benefits agreements as legally binding contracts between developers and
community organizations.

**Health Focus:** Science communication as a public health practice;
translating epidemiological findings into language that compels action;
the WHO storytelling framework for health impact; how assignment 4
presentations can be evaluated for effectiveness with non-expert
audiences.

**Data:** Synthesis of all course datasets; GitHub repository structure
for reproducible reporting; peer evaluation rubric for Assignment 4
(provided on Carmen).

**R Code:** Final polish on any Shiny app elements; GitHub CLI or
RStudio Git pane for repository commits; R Markdown framing notes for
curated lab submissions; rmarkdown::render() to batch-knit multiple lab
files.

- Screen and discuss 3-4 selected Assignment 4 presentations as class
  case studies; complete peer evaluation rubric

- Workshop: translating a regression coefficient table into 3-bullet
  executive insights for a city council memo

- GitHub lab: set up Final Portfolio repository structure (README.md,
  data/, analysis/, policy-memo/, reflection/)

- Begin drafting the new 3-page synthesis policy memo for the Final
  Portfolio
